title: The Iron Oath

identity.premise: The player leads a mercenary company in a crumbling medieval-fantasy realm, completing contracts, managing and recruiting mercenaries, and surviving a world where evil steadily grows.

setting.world_summary: Grim medieval-fantasy world divided among rival houses and factions; overland map with cities, wilderness, ruins and dungeons; an ongoing conflict against monstrous factions (black skell, wealdere, nullbeasts, voidspawn).
setting.tech_and_magic: Medieval technology; magic exists as combat abilities, enchantments and scrolls; no firearms.

tone.range: Dark, grim and serious, with dry humor in mercenary banter and light moments in camp dialogue; high-stakes survival tone in events and contracts.
localization_consequences: Keep the medieval register: avoid modern slang and corporate language.
Combat and trait text must stay concise (UI), dialogue must sound spoken.
Terms like Attack, Defense, Speed, Accuracy are core stat names: keep the PT-BR gamer register (Ataque, Defesa, Velocidade, Precisão).
Names of abilities keep original English names where they are identity-bearing (e.g. class names preserved, spell names localized when natural).

text_domains: Combat ability names and tooltips (TMP rich text with <color> and <sprite> tags)
Trait, perk and injury names and descriptions
Dialogue (dynamic dialogue JSON nodes, quest dialogue)
style_rules: Preserve <color=...> and <sprite name=...> tags exactly (they are protected tokens).
Trait and ability names use Title Case in the source: preserve a capitalized PT-BR form.
Placeholder {0} tokens move naturally inside the sentence.
British spellings in source stay British in meaning but are written in PT-BR orthography.
NPC names, house names and place names are preserved unless a natural PT-BR form exists and the glossary locks it.
Numbers, percentages, dice and duration values are always preserved exactly.
